text:
maya: Heads up — after the CUDA 12.14p3 rollout to staging we're seeing a clear small-batch latency regression on the runtime (p50 up ~25%, p95 up ~40%). KV-cache coldstart is worse too, hit-rate dipping by ~8%

dan: ugh. which images/driver exactly? any flamegraphs or perf traces yet?

maya: staging boxes now on nvidia-driver 550.9 -> 551.12 and CUDA toolchain 12.14p3. PyTorch wheel is torch==2.1.1+cu12, Triton 2.4. Logs attached in the CI run (link: https://ci.internal/reports/1745009876)

ci-bot: perf-test/staging-smallbatch failed: latency regression detected (p50: 12.8ms -> 16.1ms, p95: 36.2ms -> 50.6ms). See artifacts: https://ci.internal/artifacts/1745009876

leo: quick check — does autotune choose different matmul kernels? we had similar symptoms when nvrtc started emitting slightly different PTX and cublasLt picked another algorithm.

maya: good call. I ran a quick trace on a small repro and saw Triton autotuner flipping from cublasLt Algo 7 -> Algo 2 for 128x128 matmul on a100. nvprof shows higher kernel times after the driver bump. paste: ```
# before (driver 550.9)
matmul: Algo 7, 1.6ms
# after (driver 551.12)
matmul: Algo 2, 2.4ms
```

sara: also seeing more kernel launches (shallow batching) — batching heuristic seems to prefer smaller groups, so we're losing amortization. Any config change in the rollout?

maya: rollout just updated driver + nvrtc. No deliberate config changes. Batching metrics: average batch size down 18% in staging for tiny models. KV cache miss spike coincides with first autoupdate run.

leo: two hypotheses: 1) nvrtc/ptx layout change causing different kernels chosen at runtime; 2) driver scheduler affinity change making small batches pay kernel launch overhead. We should bisect driver and triton/pytorch.

dan: can we quickly test by pinning to prior driver on one staging node? if revert fixes, we know where to look.

maya: repro'd on single node by downgrading to 550.9 — latency and kernel algos reverted. So driver/toolchain looks causal.

ops-bot: /ticket create "staging perf regression after CUDA 12.14p3" assigned to eng-runtime, severity P1

sara: next steps from my side: capture nvprof and NVTX traces on both driver versions, collect Triton autotune tables (tuner.json) and cublasLt selection logs, and run a microbench harness for 16/32/64/128 sequences. I'll post all artifacts.

leo: also run a quick experiment: set environment TRITON_AUTOTUNE_DISABLE=1 or force our legacy matmul path so we can confirm it's kernel selection rather than scheduling. If that fixes, we can hotfix a config to stop rollout.

maya: tried TRITON_AUTOTUNE_DISABLE=1 — p50 improved back to ~13ms (almost baseline). That strongly implicates autotune + nvrtc output.

dan: ok, block the rest of rollout and pin driver to 550.9 on staging while we bisect. I'll open a revert PR for the driver upgrade in the rollout chart.

maya: filing bisect notes: compare nvrtc/ptx differences using cuobjdump -ptx on compiled kernels and diff the PTX sections. Also bisect Triton autotune table generator commit (maybe a change in PTX->kernel name mapping).

sara: I have a short profiler snippet I'll run and share (nvproftools + nsight): ```
nv-nsight-cu-cli --trace api --launch "./smallbatch_bench --seq 64 --iter 1000" > nsight_out.log
```

leo: thanks — if we confirm deterministic PTX diffs, we'll reach out to NVRTC/nvidia. If it's driver scheduler/sm-clocking, escalate to infra for node-level revert.

maya: action items: 1) dan pins driver on staging (in flight) 2) sara posts autotune tables + traces 3) leo/maiya (typo? we didn't introduce maiya) — ignore. 3) leo to run PTX diff script 4) I'll prepare a rollback pr for the rollout and notify customers.

dan: PR opened to pin driver: https://git.internal/infrastructure/rollouts/pull/421 (WIP). Leaving rollback on until we have a root cause. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks everyone. will dump the autotune jsons to the ticket and follow up with a short root-cause doc once we have the PTX diffs. :rocket:
